summary: Round 2, verifying the two test methods added to LocalSequencerAncestorSealTest.java since round 1 (hash 9ff7ae9...) close the gaps round 1's own test-reviewer (T1: the chainEpoch>=1 lower boundary was never exercised down to 0) and a concurrent peer session flagged. Confirmed the diff itself moved only by these two methods: production code (ChainReplay.java's firstInheritableAncestor, LocalSequencer.start's seal-then-open ordering) and the backlog.md M4.16/M4.32 rows are byte-identical to what round 1 already reviewed clean, and LocalSequencerFailoverTest's moved request-count assertions were also already part of round 1's diff. Ran the full sequencer module (`./gradlew :sequencer:test`): 190 tests, 0 failures/errors/skips. Independently re-derived the T1 boundary mutation rather than trusting the red-record JSON: hand-traced firstInheritableAncestor's `while (chainEpoch >= 1 && neverOpened(...))` against aWalkWithNoGenuineAncestorAnywhereStopsAtZeroRatherThanSealingAnUnopenedEpoch's fixture (epochs 1-4 all burned, epoch 4 given a Seal-at-slot-0 shape), predicted that mutating the guard to `> 1` would stop the walk at chainEpoch==1 without ever inspecting it and wrongly report epoch 1 as inheritable (successor would seal a never-opened chain and its CONTINUE would wrongly name epoch 1 instead of 0) -- then applied that exact one-line mutation to the working tree, reran the two affected test classes, and observed the predicted failure verbatim (aWalkWithNoGenuineAncestorAnywhereStopsAtZeroRatherThanSealingAnUnopenedEpoch: expected 0L but was 1L), reverted, and reran green. This closes T1 for real, not just on paper. Traced the second new test (aRedrivenSealsExtraDeltaReachesTheSuccessorProvingOrderIsLoadBearing) by hand against CommitLog.seal(): the redrive loop applies every entry it loses to before retrying, so the sequence it finally returns already reflects the zombie's in-flight delta, and that returned value is exactly what bounds ChainReplay.inherited's read via crossFrom -- confirms the test's core claim (the crossing must read AFTER the redrive resolves, not before) is real, even though the test's own comment framing ('swap seal-then-open into open-then-seal') slightly overstates it as a literal statement swap, when prevSeq's data dependency on seal()'s return makes a literal swap impossible to even compile; the substantive property under test (redrive-resolved sequence must be what bounds the cross-read) is genuine and was previously unexercised -- the existing LocalSequencerTest#aTakeoverRedrivesPastTheFencedLeadersInFlightCommitRatherThanGivingUp only asserts the Seal and CONTINUE bytes, never the successor's resumed offset, exactly the gap round 1's test-reviewer's note ('not independently exercised... would likely still pass here') identified. No object-store request added inside a loop over records/shards/partitions/indices; the walk-back and redrive are both bounded by epochs/entries already governed by NFR-9 and pinned by LocalSequencerFailoverTest's unchanged counts. No blocking or major findings; no new minors introduced by these two additions.
